title: A shared phase shift gives no clear prediction gain in short TESS models of 70 selected CPVs
abstract: We test whether one phase shift predicts changes across sharp-feature harmonics of complex periodic variables. In 1,915 released TESS window pairs from 70 stars, at a median separation of 10.42 rotations, direct odd-to-even harmonic transfer increases median phase error by 34.47%. A scale chosen on other stars gives a mean error reduction of 0.66%, with a repeated-selection 95% star-bootstrap interval from -0.84% to 2.05%. A conditional Gaussian summary simulation with shared drift of 0.0002 cycles per rotation gives a mean gain of 15.17% (7.70% to 19.94%); fixed phases give -0.36%. The observed pattern gives no clear shared-displacement gain despite sensitivity to a slow coherent shift in this error model. Unknown harmonic covariance, selected stars and use of summary fits prevent a physical speed bound. Independent cloud motion and opacity changes remain possible. Code, aggregate evidence, figures and exact input hashes are included.
